sections.h2: Who bills tax on a Waco house
sections.html:
Three parties shape a Waco tax bill. The McLennan Central Appraisal District, because the city lies in McLennan County, sets your value. Each taxing unit adopts its own rate. The McLennan County Tax Office then sends the bill and collects.

About 147,788 people live in Waco, and owners occupy 49.4% of homes. A typical owned home is valued at $221,700, with rent at a median of $1,165. Since about half the homes are rented, many owners here are landlords, and a rental house earns no homestead exemption.

One Waco address often falls under several units: McLennan County, McLennan Community College, a school district and the City of Waco, with a Waco improvement district at $0.100000 on top. Your address decides the school unit. Besides Waco ISD, the county's sheet names Midway, Connally, La Vega, China Spring, Lorena and other districts, so check which one is on your account.

  • Values, exemptions and protests: McLennan Central Appraisal District, 315 S 26th Street, Waco, which accepts homestead filings through its online portal.
  • Bills and payments: McLennan County Tax Office.
  • City rate and budget: the City of Waco's finance department.

Waco's city rate for 2026 is $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value: $0.578371 for operations plus $0.176629 for debt service. The budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 holds it at 75.5000 cents. With the rate unchanged, a different city bill means your own taxable value moved.

Every unit's total divides into operations and debt service. Waco ISD's $1.034870 is $0.763700 for operations and $0.271170 for debt, the county's $0.374805 is $0.344706 and $0.030099, and the college's $0.140715 is $0.123438 and $0.017277.

Your combined rate depends on your school district and any special district.

You may pay as soon as the bill arrives, and it becomes delinquent after January 31 of the following year. A January 31 that lands on a weekend moves the deadline to the next business day.

On February 1 the collector adds a 6% penalty and 1% interest. The penalty rises monthly to 12% by July 1, and interest has no ceiling. A unit that hires a collection attorney may add up to 20%. Seniors, disabled owners and a disabled veteran may split the bill into four installments.

  • October: bills go out from the tax office.
  • November 30: first-half deadline if you split the bill under the state rule, with the balance due by the next June 30.
  • January 31: the general due date for the full amount.
  • February 1: penalty and interest begin.

sections.h2: How to pay McLennan County property tax
sections.html:
Online payment needs your property tax account number. For in-person and mail options, ask the tax office. The online site belongs to an outside company, so take questions about it to the tax office, not the county webmaster.

Card payments carry a 2.19% fee and electronic checks a $1.50 flat fee, both going to the payment vendor. A credit card payment needs only the account number. An electronic check needs the account number and bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

The tax office runs tax sales online through GovEase, and bidders register there. An owner facing a sale should ask the tax office about redemption, which Texas limits by property type.

sections.h2: Lowering your appraisal or tax bill
sections.html:
Do you live in the house? File for the homestead exemption. Does the value look high? Protest it. Both go to the appraisal district, and most exemption applications are due before May 1.

McLennan CAD mails a notice of appraised value to owners whose market value rose at least $1,000 over the prior year. The notice lists market value, assessed value and taxable value. Market value is what the property would sell for on January 1. Assessed value reflects the homestead cap, and taxable value is what remains after exemptions.

  • Protest deadline: May 15, unless 30 days after mailing runs later.
  • Ways to file: by email, in person at 315 S 26th Street, or through the online portal, which opens for most residential property from April 10 through May 15.
  • After filing: an informal meeting with a district appraiser, then a hearing before the appraisal review board if no settlement is reached.
  • Agents: a family member or friend can represent you if you file an appointment of agent form.

Evidence is posted in the online portal, which you reach with the property owner ID and PIN printed on the notice. The review board looks at market value, so bring sales of similar nearby homes and photos of condition problems. Homestead value growth is capped at 10% a year after the first year, and seniors or disabled owners can freeze school tax.

sections.h2: Selling a Waco house with taxes due
sections.html:
Each year's tax lien exists from January 1, which is why the title company pays it at closing and prorates what remains.

Whoever owned on January 1 is liable for that year even if the sale closes in spring, and delinquent tax keeps title from being clear. If you are behind, ask the tax office for a balance covering the county, city, school district and college. Heirs left off the recorded deed can still claim the exemption with an ownership affidavit and a death certificate.

A seller with a tenant should check whether a homestead exemption was ever filed. Rental property carries none, so the seller's bill may be higher than neighbors' bills on owner-occupied homes.

The order of work matters more than speed. These steps keep the tax account from becoming the reason a closing slips.

  1. Ask the tax office for a balance covering the county, city, school district and college.
  2. Check your account for any improvement district charge on top of the standard units.
  3. Confirm whether a homestead exemption is on file, or whether the house was a rental.
  4. Tell the title company about any open protest, since the value may still change.
  5. Send the title company the payoff figures so it can settle the year's tax and prorate the rest at closing.

A cash buyer does not need a bank's appraisal and approval, so the closing date follows the title work. If taxes are behind, the balance comes out of your proceeds. You do not have to bring cash to the table to sell.

faqs.q: What is the Waco city property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value for 2026, split between $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt. The adopted budget keeps it at 75.5000 cents.

faqs.q: What is the Waco ISD homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Waco ISD gives $140,000 to homesteads and $200,000 to seniors and disabled owners, at a total rate of 1.034870.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Waco property tax in February?
faqs.a: Yes. A balance left after January 31 is delinquent, and February 1 brings a 6% penalty plus 1% interest, with the penalty rising each month to 12% in July.

faqs.q: Can I protest my McLennan County appraisal online?
faqs.a: Yes, for most residential property. The district's portal runs April 10 to May 15, and the deadline is May 15 unless 30 days after mailing runs later.

faqs.q: Does a Waco rental house get a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption needs an owner who lives there as a main residence on January 1, with no second homestead claimed elsewhere. A rental is taxed without it.
